sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cryo-EM structure of CCK1R/mGsqi complex determined at high resolution, confirming receptor folding, membrane insertion, and G-protein coupling; surface expression and functional G-protein complex formation confirmed.
sites.rationale: CCKAR has no signal peptide (topology residues 1–41 are extracellular); residue 1 (M) is the mature N-terminus. The FLAG tag in the L1/L2/L3 construct is placed N-terminal to the CCK1R sequence after HA-signal cleavage, placing it on the extracellular face. The 3C protease site allows removal of the N-terminal modifications, confirming the receptor itself is intact and functional. Python confirmed residue 1 = M and TM1 begins at residue 42, giving 42 residues of clearance from the tag position to the first TM helix. Full-length human CCK1R was engineered with an HA signal sequence, N-terminal FLAG tag, and 22 aa of M4 mAChR N-terminus prepended before the receptor sequence, plus a C-terminal 8xHis tag, expressed as a membrane-anchored receptor for cryo-EM structural studies of the CCK1R/G-protein complex (PMC8208569). The HA signal is cleaved post-translationally, leaving the FLAG tag on the extracellular N-terminus. No specific CCK1R residue number is named for the FLAG junction; the N-terminus (residue 1, M) is the sole extracellular terminus, so insert_after_residue=0 is topology-derived.

sources.claim: Human WT CCK1R was modified to include an N-terminal hemagglutinin (HA) signal sequence, FLAG-tag, 22 amino acids of the N-terminus of the M 4 muscarinic receptor to improve expression [ 28 , 29 ], a 3C-protease recognition sequence to remove the N-terminal modifications, and a carboxyl-terminal 8xhistadine (8xHis) tag ( S1A Fig ).

literature_notes: L1, L2, and L3 all describe the same N-terminal FLAG-tagged CCK1R construct from PMC8208569; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip. L4 (PMC8604728) describes a second independent N-terminal tagging of CCK-AR (HA-signal + 8xHis + double-MBP + TEV + receptor), corroborating that the extracellular N-terminus tolerates large N-terminal additions; it is not listed as a separate site because it pins the same junction (insert_after_residue=0) and L1 already grounds it with higher functional validation. L8 (PMC13485628) describes FLAG-tagged Aplysia CCKAR (apCCKR) mutants with surface expression comparable to WT, but no residue position is stated and the protein is a non-human ortholog; it provides indirect corroboration but cannot independently ground a site. The C-terminal miniSOG fusion (L5/L6/L7) is placed in other_positions because the C-terminus of CCKAR is intracellular (residues 374–428 per topology landmarks). No ledger line supports an insertion in ECL1 (105–115), ECL2 (179–210), or ECL3 (335–349) of human CCKAR.

literature_other_positions.note: miniSOG fused to the C-terminus of CCK1R and expressed in CHO-K1 cells; photodynamic activation triggered calcium oscillations confirming functional surface receptor, but the C-terminus (residues 374–428) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this is not an extracellular surface tag site.
